name: KY-004 push button module
description: Push button: a 6x6 mm tactile switch between S and GND with a 10 kOhm pull-up resistor from S to the + pin. S is HIGH while the button is released and goes LOW while it is held (active low). Runs on 3.3-5 V. Some other KY-004 clones wire the resistor as a pull-down (HIGH when pressed); this part models the pull-up board. Sold as: Joy-IT KY-004 button module (black 3-pin SensorKit board with black tactile button; header S, + (middle), -).
eli5: A little button on a board: when you press it, your board can tell.

pins.name: S
pins.description: Signal (pin 1): HIGH while released, LOW while the button is held. Pulled up to + by the on-board 10 kOhm resistor.
Middle pin: supply for the pull-up, 3.3-5 V. Use 3V3 with an ESP32 or Pico, because S is pulled up to this voltage.

buildNotes: On an ESP32 or Pico connect + to 3V3: the on-board 10 kOhm pull-up takes S to the + voltage, so 5 V on + puts 5 V on the GPIO.
S is active LOW on the Joy-IT board: 1 while released, 0 while pressed.
Check your board first: some KY-004 clones use the resistor as a pull-down (S reads 0 at rest, 1 when pressed). Use KY004(pin, active_low=False) for those.
The contacts bounce at each press; debounce for about 20 ms (the driver's pressed() does this).

example.code:
from ky004 import KY004
import time

button = KY004({S})
while True:
    print('Button: %s' % ('PRESSED' if button.pressed() else 'released'))
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports a press while the button is held

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
